sentences.text: The Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates destination consultation when a patient’s condition or the operating status of a facility may affect the assignment.
The consultation uses the patient’s reported condition, transport estimate, and current facility acceptance information available to the Regional Dispatch Center.
The Regional Medical Director provides clinical guidance when destination selection involves a specialized capability or a regional care protocol.
The Hospital Liaison Desk contacts the Emergency Department to confirm whether the proposed destination can receive the patient.
The Regional Dispatch Center uses the correction slip to reconcile a reported destination change with the active incident record.
Larkspur confirms the incident identifier and intended receiving facility before the destination request is transmitted.
The Emergency Department advises the Hospital Liaison Desk of relevant capacity limits, access constraints, or changes to its receiving status.
The Hospital Liaison Desk records the consultation outcome and communicates any destination restriction to the Regional Dispatch Center.
The Regional Dispatch Center evaluates the consultation outcome against patient acuity, transport time, and available ambulance coverage.
The Ambulance Coordination Platform presents the approved destination and any associated operational instructions to dispatch staff.
The Radio Coordinator relays destination instructions to the Paramedic Crew over the Regional Radio Network.
The Paramedic Crew acknowledges the destination and advises dispatch if conditions require renewed consultation.
The South Gate Status Board produces the South Access Lane Notice when the south approach has a material access constraint.
The South Gate Status Board displays current access information for crews approaching the receiving facility through the south entrance.
The Shift Commander reviews access constraints that could affect arrival timing or safe patient transfer.
The Regional Radio Network supports updates between dispatch and the Paramedic Crew while the ambulance is en route.
Call Taker Mara receives the Bedside Arrival Receipt to support completion of the incident record.
Call Taker Mara verifies that the recorded arrival time is consistent with the dispatch timeline and crew communications.
Ambulance Unit 417 reports arrival at the receiving facility and confirms when patient handover is complete.
The Emergency Department and the Paramedic Crew clarify any discrepancy in patient identity or transfer documentation before the crew clears the facility.
The Data Quality Officer reviews incomplete arrival or handover fields during routine record-quality checks.
The Regional Dispatch Center updates the incident status after receiving confirmation that the patient has been transferred to facility care.
The Hospital Liaison Desk remains available to resolve facility-level questions that arise during or immediately after handover.
The Shift Commander escalates unresolved destination or access issues through established regional coordination procedures.
